2	==================================================================================================
3	
4	ROLE: You are the principal engineer for AGH, working in Plan Mode with gpt-5.5 xhigh reasoning. This is a
5	large, long-running redesign round — exactly what Plan Mode and your model tier exist for. Investigate
6	first (the required reading below is dense and load-bearing), then present ONE implementation plan that
7	sequences the full scope into ordered, independently verifiable phases. After approval you implement
8	hands-off until completion.
9	
10	This round builds ON TOP of the already-landed Round 1 (thread-membership routing + prompt-cost
11	accounting — committed on main; plan at .claude/plans/2026-07-01-network-thread-routing-cost-round1.md).
12	Round 1 is a prerequisite, not a draft: do not revert or re-litigate it. Where this round intentionally
13	REVERSES one Round 1 default (see D1 below), it does so as an explicit, documented hard cut.
14	
15	--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
16	PRODUCT FRAME (decided by the operator — these are constraints, not options)
17	--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
18	
19	AGH separates two planes:
20	
21	- CONVERSATION PLANE (network channels/threads): collaborative and cheap. Threads exist for deciding,
22	  reviewing, analyzing, planning, and discussing. Agents respond in a short, conversational register.
23	  Read-only lookups to answer a question are fine; heavy or mutating execution is NOT done in threads.
24	- EXECUTION PLANE (kanban tasks + autonomy kernel): owns real work. When a thread conversation produces
25	  actionable work, it is PROMOTED into a kanban task carrying a compact digest + pointer back to the
26	  thread. The kernel orchestrates execution — including fanning one task into N sub-runs of the SAME
27	  agent definition with DIFFERENT designation briefs — and compact status flows back into the
28	  originating thread as conversation.
29	
30	The bridge between the planes is first-class and agent-manageable. The golden register rule that must
31	reach agents through guidance: "threads are for deciding and discussing — reply short and conversational;
32	when actionable work emerges, promote it to a task and link the card; do not execute inside the thread."
33

36	--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

48	   implementation map for the bridge + execution plane: CreateTaskFromPeer (ZERO non-test callers today),
49	   withNetworkRunMetadata precedent, designation-brief seam (TaskRunPromptOverlay → opts.PromptOverlay →

73	--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
74	
75	A. CONVERSATION-PLANE EFFICIENCY
76	
77	A1. Channel activation policy (the "never a black hole" fix — reverses Round 1's zero-delivery default
78	    as an explicit hard cut):
79	    - New store-backed per-channel setting fanout_policy: 'capability_match' (DEFAULT) | 'coordinator' |
80	      'all_members'. Persist on network_channels (migration v44; map 08 area 1 has all four SQL
81	      touchpoints + NetworkChannelEntry + validation + PATCH route precedent).
82	    - Activation evaluation inside the delivery-set computation (router.go deliveriesFromLocalPeers, the
83	      site map 08 pins): for an UNADDRESSED thread message with no recorded participants, evaluate the
84	      channel policy instead of returning zero deliveries.
85	    - capability_match: deterministic, no-LLM matcher (new internal/network/activation.go) tokenizing
86	      SayBody.Intent (fallback Text) against each LocalPeer.CapabilityCatalog ID/Summary using the
87	      existing containment primitives (matchesWhoisQuery family). Top-K bounded (K configurable,
88	      sensible default 3). If no match → digest fallback to thread/channel members — NEVER silently
89	      nothing, NEVER all-members full injection.
90	    - coordinator: route the message as a full injection to the channel's coordinator peer. You must
91	      design the coordinator signal (none exists on PeerCard/LocalPeer today — map 08 flags it):
92	      prefer an explicit capability tag or channel-settings field over name conventions. The
93	      coordinator's job in conversation is triage: answer, pull in peers via mentions, or promote to task.
94	    - all_members: today's full fan-out, for small channels that opt in.
95	    - Mentions always override policy (see A2). Policy decisions must be observable (audit/log/hook —
96	      including which peers were activated and why) and agent-manageable (see A4 verbs + PATCH).
97	
98	A2. Mentions (multi-target addressing):
99	    - Add Envelope.Mentions []string. KEEP To (it drives DirectRoomIdentity and directed semantics) —
100	      mentions are thread-plane multi-target addressing; map 08 lists the full blast radius
101	      (envelope/validate/router/cloneEnvelope/parseEnvelopeSummary/promptNetworkMeta/XML attrs/
102	      networkLogFields/contracts/CLI --mention/tool schema/tests/docs). Mention-only envelopes stay on
103	      the broadcast subject with receiver-side filtering (subjectForEnvelope must NOT flip to
104	      DirectSubject).
105	    - Mentioned peers get full injection and become thread participants (upsert like peer_to in Round 1).
106	
107	A3. Delivery composition diet + digest batching (slices 03 + map 08):
108	    - Suppress protocolGuidanceText after first successful exposure per session with a DURABLE ledger
109	      (survives reconnect/dropSession — Round 1's in-memory taper resets today).
110	    - Collapse the reply-flags prose: verify first whether PromptNetworkMeta reaches model-visible
111	      context across provider adapters; if it does not, keep ONE compact line referencing the ids in the
112	      message metadata instead of the ~400 B flag enumeration. Design honestly around what you verify.
113	    - Stop double-encoding say bodies: plaintext only for chat say; base64 body only for structured kinds
114	      (capability/receipt/trace) where exact-bytes fidelity matters. Preserve an observability path for
115	      canonical bytes (audit already stores them).
116	    - Digest delivery mode: new DeliveryMode "digest" + a multi-envelope digest formatter (renderer is
117	      strictly per-envelope today). Used for (a) policy digest-fallback (A1) and (b) coalescing a
118	      backed-up per-session queue into one turn while preserving per-message ids for reply/causation.
119	      Rework prompt-cost attribution (recordThreadPeerPromptCost assumes 1 delivery = 1 envelope) so
120	      digest turns attribute cost honestly across the coalesced envelopes.
121	    - Extend injected-body caps for non-say kinds (greet/capability precedent: greet_summary 160-rune cap).
122	
123	A4. Volume verbs + subscriptions:
124	    - New network_subscriptions store (migration v45) keyed (workspace_id, channel, thread_id, peer_id)
125	      with mode mute|digest|full + optional keyword filters. Daemon-side, zero-token evaluation at the
126	      delivery-set site (resolver-interface precedent: ThreadParticipantResolver injection).
127	    - Verbs with three-surface parity (native tool + CLI + HTTP/UDS): mute / unmute / subscribe /
128	      digest-mode per channel and per thread. Workspace-scoped; hook-observable.
129	    - Channel settings PATCH (fanout_policy + defaults) for operators AND agents.
130	
131	A5. Response-register shaping (slice 06 — operator-mandated):
132	    - One short surface-aware register line inside the per-delivery guidance, riding the existing
133	      verbose→compact taper (do NOT re-inflate what A3 just cut — budget the line).
134	    - A StartupPredicate-gated, Budget-capped network-etiquette startup section via ComposedAssembler
135	      (wired in boot.go beside Situation/Memory/Skills), active only for sessions that join channels.
136	    - Turn-source-aware guidance at the pre-submit / input-augmenter seam using TurnSourceNetwork where
137	      per-delivery text is not enough.
138	    - The register content encodes: conversational brevity; reply only when addressed/activated or you
139	      add value; thread etiquette (address peers, reference message ids); and the two-planes golden rule
140	      (promote actionable work to a task instead of executing in-thread — see B).
141	    - "Response register" section in skills/agh/references/network.md; guidance sizing config-driven
142	      (NextRoundGuidanceMaxBytes precedent). Register shaping is GUIDANCE ONLY — never a wire-level cap
143	      on SayBody.Text (breaks receipt+trace+say flows and long handoffs).
144	
145	B. TWO-PLANES BRIDGE
146	
147	B1. Thread→task promotion (first-class verb, three-surface parity):
148	    - Extend the task-create path so a task can carry a typed thread origin: channel, thread_id,
149	      originating message id, and a byte-budgeted pin-and-trim digest (enforceTaskContextBudget
150	      precedent) + pointer. Never full-history replay.
151	    - Wire the network ingress: CreateTaskFromPeer exists, is capability-gated, and has ZERO non-test
152	      callers — add the wire dispatch that reaches it, mirroring withNetworkRunMetadata to stamp trusted
153	      thread metadata server-side.
154	    - Surfaces: native tool (agh__task_promote_from_thread or equivalent), CLI (agh task promote), HTTP
155	      (thread-scoped promote route). Promote CREATES a task (kanban card) — it does not auto-execute
156	      unless it goes through the explicit enqueue path (respect Task.AutoEnqueueOnReady semantics).
157	    - Web: the thread view exposes promote + shows the linked card; the kanban card links back to the
158	      thread (scope web work to what the changed contracts require plus these two affordances).
159	
160	B2. Status-back:
161	    - A network status-back EventObserver registered in composeTaskEventObserver, imitating
162	      bridgeTerminalTaskNotificationObserver (filter, de-dupe, deliver): on meaningful transitions of a
163	      thread-originated task, post ONE compact conversational message into the originating thread
164	      (state, run id, blocker/next action, artifact link) following the Communication Discipline register.
165	    - Design the missing primitive: daemon-originated network message injection (Manager.Send is
166	      session-bound today). Prefer an explicit system/runtime peer identity that is first-class and
167	      observable (identity/proof rules in internal/CLAUDE.md apply) over impersonating any session.
168	
169	C. EXECUTION PLANE — DESIGNATED SUB-RUNS
170	
171	C1. Fan-out: a task-service API (e.g. FanOutRuns) that enqueues N runs of one task via the authoritative
172	    EnqueueRun path — one run per designation — each with designation brief (+ index/group) in run
173	    metadata. Do NOT repurpose parent_run_id (review lineage) or previous_run_id (retry lineage); if
174	    explicit sibling grouping is needed, add designation_group_id via append-only migration. task_runs
175	    stays a single queue; ClaimNextRun stays authoritative; the scheduler never claims.
176	C2. Briefs: render the designation brief into the per-run prompt overlay via bundleForRun →
177	    renderTaskBundlePrompt (the TaskRunPromptOverlay → opts.PromptOverlay → manager_start seam is
178	    confirmed end-to-end; coordinator sessions pick the brief up automatically via coordinator_runtime).
179	C3. Budgets + stop: per-run budget caps (new state — design the minimal honest shape; RuntimeLimits and
180	    SessionSpawnBudget are the precedents) and an explicit quiescence condition: all designated runs
181	    terminal → task-level rollup runs → status-back fires. Bound N (config default, hard ceiling).
182	C4. Aggregation: task-level rollup composing sibling-run Results (priorRunSummaries precedent) into a
183	    task artifact the status-back message links.
184	C5. Surfaces + guidance: fan-out reachable via task tool/CLI/HTTP surfaces (parity), and
185	    skills/agh/references/tasks-and-orchestration.md updated (fan-out ladder, designation briefs,
186	    aggregation, status-back register).
187	
188	D. CROSS-CUTTING DECISIONS AND RULES
189	
190	D1. Explicit hard cut vs Round 1: unaddressed-thread zero-delivery is REPLACED by policy evaluation with
191	    digest fallback. Document as a hard cut: update the Round-1-rewritten docs/skill sections and delete
192	    superseded guidance/tests (list delete targets in the plan).
193	D2. Hook payload enrichment: add size/estimated-token fields to NetworkPayload hook events (extensions
194	    can observe cost); activation decisions and subscriptions emit hook/audit events.
195	D3. Config lifecycle: new keys only where truly global (e.g. activation top-K default, digest cadence,
196	    guidance size, fan-out N ceiling) — per-channel state is store-backed, not config. Register every
197	    new key with defaults + validation + docs; keep cost knobs distinct from safety bounds.
198	D4. Migrations: append-only, numbered, re-verify the tail at HEAD before numbering (expect v44/v45+...).
199	    Update the migration-tail test assertion. Fresh-DB schema and migrations must agree.
200	D5. Contracts: every payload/request change co-ships codegen (make codegen; make codegen-check).
201	D6. Workspace isolation: every new datum (policy, subscriptions, thread origin, designation group,
202	    status-back) is workspace-scoped with leak-proof tests.
203	D7. Tests: extend canonical suites (router_test, delivery_test, manager_test, store/globaldb migration
204	    tests, api handler tests with status+body, task manager tests). Test decisions per
205	    consolidate-test-suites — no filler regression files, no prose/snapshot tests.
206	D8. Docs: skills/agh references (network.md, tasks-and-orchestration.md) + packages/site protocol and
207	    runtime network/tasks pages updated in the same cut.
208	D9. AGH Impact Audit (4 rows: Native tools / Extensibility and hooks / Workspace data isolation /
209	    Official AGH skill) required in the plan AND the completion report.
210	
211	OUT OF SCOPE (do not plan these): NATS transport/subject changes (thread-scoped subjects remain a
212	possible future wire cut — note it, don't do it); turn-taking/floor-control and listener-interruption
213	mechanics; LLM-based or RL-based routing/scoring (the matcher is deterministic); CRDT substrates;
214	provider TokenUsage attribution joins (estimated size/tokens remain the network-side measure); web
215	redesign beyond changed contracts + the named affordances (mention picker, policy visibility/settings,
216	promote button + card/thread links).
217	
218	--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
219	PLAN EXPECTATIONS
220	--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
221	
222	- Sequence the scope into ordered phases with explicit dependencies (a sensible shape: schema/store →
223	  wire+routing/policy → delivery diet+digest → verbs/config → register guidance → bridge (promote +
224	  status-back) → designated sub-runs → web + docs — but you own the final sequencing and may split
225	  differently with justification).
226	- Per phase: files touched, migrations, delete targets, tests extended, and the verification commands.
227	- Name the product decisions you are locking (default fanout_policy=capability_match with digest

234	(fan-out seam only), internal/daemon (task_event_bridge_notifier, coordinator_runtime, native_tools,
235	boot prompt sections, runtime_prompt), internal/session (prompt path/overlay only), internal/acp
236	(PromptNetworkMeta), internal/situation (task_context), internal/config, internal/store (+ globaldb
237	migrations), internal/api (+ contract codegen), internal/tools + internal/toolruntime, internal/cli,
238	skills/agh references, packages/site network+tasks docs, web/src/systems/network + web/src/systems/tasks

240	worktree changes (docs/design/opendesign/*, .compozy/tasks/feature-stories/*).
241	
242	VERIFICATION: make verify must pass end-to-end before you report done. Focused iteration per package

244	completion with a phase-by-phase diff summary + verification evidence; the controller owns commits.

1	# AGH Network Token Optimization Megaround
2	
3	## Summary
4	
5	Implement the packet as a hard-cut redesign that separates the conversation plane from the execution plane:
6	
7	- Conversation threads decide, discuss, review, and promote work; they do not execute heavy or mutating work directly.
8	- Actionable thread work is promoted into kanban tasks with typed origin links, compact digest context, and task/run status posted back to the source thread.
9	- Network deliveries become cheaper and more targeted through mention-aware routing, channel fanout policy, durable delivery guidance suppression, digest mode, subscriptions, and a short response register.
10	
11	No compatibility bridges or aliases will be added.
12	
13	## Implementation Changes
14	
15	### 1. Schema, Config, and Contracts
16	
17	- Append migrations after the current v43 tail:
18	  - v44: add `network_channels.fanout_policy`, `network_channels.coordinator_peer_id`, and `network_timeline_log.mentions_json`.
19	  - v45: add `network_subscriptions` keyed by `(workspace_id, channel, thread_id, peer_id)` plus `network_delivery_guidance_state` for durable per-session guidance suppression.
20	  - v46: add `network_task_thread_origins` keyed by `task_id`, with `workspace_id`, `channel`, `thread_id`, `origin_message_id`, compact digest, source message IDs, and timestamps.
21	  - v47: add `task_runs.designation_group_id`, an index on `(task_id, designation_group_id)`, and a small `task_designation_rollups` table keyed by designation group.
22	- Add config defaults:
23	  - `network.activation_top_k = 3`
24	  - `network.digest_flush_interval = 250ms`
25	  - `network.digest_max_envelopes = 10`
26	  - `network.response_guidance_max_bytes = 512`
27	  - `network.delivery_structured_body_max_bytes = 4096`
28	  - `task.orchestration.designated_run_max = 5`, validated in range `1..5`
29	- Extend public contracts and regenerate OpenAPI/types with `make codegen`:
30	  - `mentions []string` on network send requests, send payloads, envelopes, timeline messages, and prompt metadata.
31	  - `fanout_policy` and `coordinator_peer_id` on channel create/detail/update payloads.
32	  - subscription payloads with `mode: mute|digest|full` and optional `keyword_filters`.
33	  - task thread origin payloads and designated fan-out run payloads.
34	- Add or update HTTP/UDS surfaces:
35	  - `PATCH /api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/network/channels/{channel}` for fanout policy and coordinator.
36	  - channel/thread subscription list, set, and delete routes.
37	  - `POST /api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/network/channels/{channel}/threads/{thread_id}/promote`.
38	  - `POST /api/tasks/{task_id}/runs/fan-out`.
39	- Add or update native tools and CLI:
40	  - update `agh__network_send` and `agh network send` with repeatable `--mention`.
41	  - add channel update, subscribe, mute, unmute, and digest-mode tools/commands.
42	  - add `agh__task_promote_from_thread` and `agh task promote`.
43	  - add `agh__task_fanout_runs` and `agh task fan-out`.
44	
45	### 2. Conversation Plane Routing and Delivery Diet
46	
47	- Replace the current zero-delivery branch for unaddressed empty-participant threads with a deterministic activation resolver:
48	  - `capability_match` is the default channel policy.
49	  - `coordinator` routes to the configured `coordinator_peer_id`; missing or unavailable coordinator falls back to digest.
50	  - `all_members` is explicit opt-in and full-injects all eligible local peers.
51	- Capability matching is token-free and deterministic:
52	  - Use `SayBody.Intent` when present, otherwise `SayBody.Text`.
53	  - Score each local peer by normalized term overlap against capability ID and summary.
54	  - Select up to `network.activation_top_k` peers with positive scores, tie-breaking by peer ID.
55	  - If no peer matches, emit a digest fallback to eligible thread/channel subscribers and record an observable activation decision.
56	- Add mention semantics:
57	  - `Envelope.Mentions []string` is normalized, deduplicated, validated as peer IDs, cloned, logged, summarized, and rendered in prompt metadata/XML attrs.
58	  - Mention-only messages remain broadcast subjects; `subjectForEnvelope` stays direct only for `To`.
59	  - Mentioned peers receive full injection, become durable thread participants, and override fanout/digest defaults; `mute` suppresses only unmentioned/unaddressed traffic.
60	- Add subscription resolution at the delivery-set site:
61	  - Most-specific thread row wins over channel row.
62	  - Empty `keyword_filters` means always applicable.
63	  - Non-empty filters are lowercased substring guards over intent/text; if no filter matches, resolution falls through to the less-specific/default rule.
64	  - `mute` suppresses matching unmentioned traffic, `digest` converts matching full traffic to digest, and `full` preserves full injection.
65	- Add `DeliveryMode` with `full`, `queued`, and `digest`, plus activation/subscription reason fields for audit and hooks.
66	- Replace prompt bloat:
67	  - `say` bodies render as escaped plain text, not base64 JSON.
68	  - structured non-say bodies remain base64 JSON but are capped by `network.delivery_structured_body_max_bytes`.
69	  - protocol/reply guidance is suppressed through durable `network_delivery_guidance_state`, surviving reconnect and `dropSession`.
70	  - prompt metadata remains visible; if any adapter path cannot expose metadata, keep a compact in-band line rather than expanding guidance.
71	- Add digest formatting:
72	  - queue backlog and activation fallback can coalesce up to `network.digest_max_envelopes` into one digest prompt after `network.digest_flush_interval`.
73	  - prompt cost attribution is allocated across included envelopes by canonical envelope size, so totals match actual digest prompt cost instead of charging each envelope as if it received a full injection.
74	- Extend hook/audit payloads with activation reason, delivery mode, prompt size bytes, estimated tokens, digest envelope count, and subscription decision.
75	
76	### 3. Response Register and Execution Plane Bridge
77	
78	- Add a startup-gated, budget-capped network etiquette section through `ComposedAssembler`:
79	  - only active for network-capable sessions.
80	  - bounded by `network.response_guidance_max_bytes`.
81	  - states the golden rule: threads decide/discuss; actionable work is promoted to tasks; replies are short and only when addressed, activated, or adding value.
82	- Add a `TurnSourceNetwork` input augmenter:
83	  - one compact line before network prompts.

5	Repo-wide rules (Critical Rules, Workflow, Build, Commits, Skill Dispatch, Memory & Skills RFC, CI/Release) live in the **root `CLAUDE.md`**. This file owns architecture, package boundaries, autonomy contracts, security invariants, and `internal/`-specific debugging/forensics.
6	
7	## Architecture
8	
9	### Principles
10	
11	- **Designed for incremental extension** — new capabilities arrive as new packages wired into `daemon/`, without modifying existing packages. Small interfaces + dependency injection. Every capability plan decides which extension points, hooks, capabilities, tools/resources, bundles, registries, bridge SDKs, and docs must be added, updated, or removed.
12	- **Pragmatic Flat with Discipline** — packages under `internal/`, API transports grouped under `api/`, no domain/infra split, no event bus.
13	- **`daemon/` is the sole composition root** — the only package that imports all others. Reconciliation logic running at boot belongs to composition root and is not "legacy support".
14	- **No package imports `daemon/`, `api/`, or `cli/`** — dependencies flow downward only.
15	- **Interfaces defined where consumed** (Go-style) — `session/` defines `AgentDriver`, `acp/` implements it.
16	- **Direct function calls through interfaces** — no event bus, no reflection-based routing, no NATS as inter-package coordination. NATS is permitted **only** inside `internal/network` as the embedded wire transport for the AGH Network protocol; daemon packages communicate via interfaces and the Notifier pattern, never by publishing to subjects.
17	- **Notifier pattern for fan-out** — typed interface for observability and SSE, not a generic bus.
18	- **No back-pointers between packages** — inject callbacks or interfaces.
19	- **Functional options for constructors** — `NewManager(opts ...Option)`.
20	- **Maps for <10 items** — no registry interfaces for small collections.
21	- **File-level organization** within packages — sub-packages only when complexity justifies it.
22	- **CI-enforceable boundaries** — `mage Boundaries` rules prevent import cycles. Update `magefile.go` Boundaries() in the same commit that introduces a new `internal/api/*` subpackage.
23	- **Build/CI plumbing tests are exceptional.** Do not parse `.github`, `Makefile`, `magefile.go`, `package.json`, or `turbo.json` to pin exact commands unless the command is a public operator/agent entry point or release contract. Prefer real or dry-run command smoke (`make -n`, `mage -l`, `make verify`, `make codegen-check`, `goreleaser check`) and assert observable lane behavior. Literal script tests must name the contract they protect.
24	- **`internal/api/core` is the canonical handler home.** REST/UDS endpoints exist as shared `BaseHandlers` methods; HTTP and UDS only choose registration and authentication. No transport-duplicated parsing/validation.
25	- **Authoritative primitives are exclusive.** When a primitive owns a state transition (`task.Service.ClaimNextRun`, `Spawn`, `EnsureMigration`), no peer package may replicate it. Wake/observe/sweep are allowed; claim/own is not. The mechanical scheduler does not call `ClaimNextRun`.
26	- **Hooks are typed dispatch, not an event bus.** Dispatch at the call site that owns the state transition. Never tail event/log tables to fire hooks. Hooks may deny/narrow/annotate but cannot bypass safety primitives (claim tokens, leases, TTL, lineage, spawn caps, permission narrowing).
27	- **Agent-manageable by default.** User-visible runtime capabilities must expose stable machine-readable control surfaces for agents: CLI verbs with `-o json`/`-o jsonl` where relevant, HTTP/UDS parity when state crosses the daemon boundary, discoverable status/config output, and docs that describe the agent path. UI-only manageability is incomplete.
28	- **No partial-surface completions.** Any change touching a public surface closes the loop end-to-end in one pass: contract → HTTP handler → UDS handler → CLI client → CLI command → extension/config/docs surfaces → tests → docs.
29	
30	### Concurrency
31	
32	Generic Go concurrency patterns (goroutine ownership, channels vs mutexes, `select`/`ctx.Done()` discipline, no `time.Sleep` in orchestration) live in `agh-code-guidelines`. Architectural invariants below are load-bearing for design decisions:
33	
34	- **Goroutines spawned by `internal/session/manager_*.go` MUST be tracked by Manager-owned WaitGroup and joined in Manager shutdown.** Never put goroutine-owned channels in a struct field that another goroutine mutates — use a per-run handle.
35	- **Detached execution lifetime.** Any work that outlives an HTTP/UDS request — prompts, network channel sends, automation jobs — MUST detach via `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)`. Never tie execution lifetime to request lifetime. Expose explicit cancel endpoints (e.g., `POST /api/workspaces/:workspace_id/sessions/:id/prompt/cancel`).
36	- **`context.WithoutCancel` does NOT preserve deadlines.** Re-attach a deadline if needed.
37	- **Subprocess managed-stop** must respect `ctx.Done()` between Shutdown and Wait. Wrap `proc.Wait()` in `select { case <-proc.Done(): case <-ctx.Done(): }`.
38	- **Process-group supervision parity.** Unix uses process groups; Windows uses forced-exit fallback. Always cross-build with `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build` before claiming subprocess work complete. Centralize signaling helpers in `internal/procutil`.
39	
40	### Runtime
41	
42	- Single-binary and local-first. Sidecars or external control planes require a written techspec.
43	- Keep execution paths deterministic and observable.
44	- **Daemon runs in background by default.** No daemon should require a foreground terminal.
45	- **`compozy exec` is headless.** `--format text` returns a single string; `--format json` returns a stream of valid JSON objects; the TUI is opt-in via `--tui`. `exec` does not persist artifacts to `.compozy/runs/` unless `--persist` is given.
46	- **Agent operations must not depend on the web UI.** If agents need to inspect, configure, start, stop, approve, claim, release, or repair a capability, the spec must provide a CLI/HTTP/UDS path with structured output and deterministic errors.
47	
48	### Observability
49	
50	- Every domain operation emits a canonical event with correlation keys (`workspace_id`, `session_id`, `parent_session_id`, `root_session_id`, `agent_name`, `task_id`, `run_id`, `claim_token_hash`, `lease_until`, `workflow_id`, `coordinator_session_id`, `scheduler_reason`, `hook_event`, `hook_name`, `spawn_depth`, `actor_kind`, `actor_id`, `release_reason`).
51	- Cover with a coverage matrix test that fails if any required lifecycle path doesn't emit its canonical event.
52	- Append-only event store (`runtime.db`) is the canonical operational ledger; session DBs are projections, not authority.
53	- Live broadcasters publish only after durable append; reconnect/replay uses `after_seq`.
54	
55	### Persistence
56	
57	- **SQLite migration registries are append-only.** `internal/store/globaldb.globalSchemaMigrations` and equivalent registries persist `version`, `name`, and `checksum` in `schema_migrations`; never insert, reorder, rename, renumber, or change an existing migration identity after it may have been applied.
58	- **Migration drift fixes require observed-history tests.** Cover fresh DB, upgrade/reopen, and the real recorded migration prefix that failed. Integrity mismatch is a safety signal to preserve, not an error to suppress.
59	- **New schema work appends at the registry tail.** If a migration appears to need an earlier slot, stop and write an ADR-backed repair plan instead of silently shifting recorded history.
60	
61	## Security Invariants
62	
63	- **`claim_token` redaction is non-negotiable.** Raw `claim_token` (`agh_claim_*`), MCP auth tokens, OAuth codes, PKCE verifiers, and secret bindings MUST NEVER appear in logs, status APIs, settings views, error payloads, channel messages, SSE, web UI, or memory. Use hash forms (`claim_token_hash`) over the wire. Network layer rejects raw `claim_token` in metadata.
64	- **Symlink escape hardening.** Skill sidecars, skill files, managed-extension dependency copies, and bundle install paths MUST verify resolved targets remain inside approved roots. Use `EvalSymlinks` + path-prefix check, not naive joins. Handle macOS `/private/var/folders` quirk (canonicalize source root before containment check).
65	- **Path security helpers.** Filesystem helpers resolving user-controlled or agent-controlled paths use the `sanitizePathKey` + `realpathDeepestExisting` pattern (defenses against null-byte, URL-encoded traversal, Unicode normalization, symlink-escape).
66	- **Identity proof-stripping defense.** In any signed-message processing path (AGH Network v1), an identity in verified format (`nickname@fingerprint`) without valid `proof` MUST classify as `rejected`, not `unverified`.
67	- **External-call timeouts.** Outbound HTTP/network calls MUST use a client with an explicit timeout. `http.DefaultClient` is forbidden in production code paths.
68	- **Load-time security scan.** Every non-bundled skill is scanned via `internal/skills.VerifyContent` on every load (not just install). Critical findings block; warning findings log; info findings log silently. Bundled skills are exempt because `go:embed` provides immutability.
69	- **Provider auth boundary.** Native ACP providers (`auth_mode = native_cli`) use provider-owned
70	  CLI login/session state and MUST NOT require AGH-bound API-key `credential_slots`. Bound secrets
71	  are legal only under `auth_mode = bound_secret`, where AGH resolves `env:` or
72	  `vault:providers/<provider>/<slot>` refs and injects exactly those values. Provider env/home
73	  policy is part of this security boundary: `env_policy = filtered` strips secret-shaped daemon
74	  variables, `env_policy = isolated` starts from a minimal allowlist, and
75	  `home_policy = isolated` points providers at `$AGH_HOME/providers/<provider>` without copying
76	  operator credentials.

139	## Memory & Skills Runtime (RFC-backed)
140	
141	- **Five-layer skill/memory/agent precedence**: Bundled → Marketplace → User → Additional → Workspace, with agent-local overriding all. Higher precedence wins on collision; an audit trail logs every shadow.

144	- **Lifecycle hooks** (`on_session_created`, `on_session_stopped`) execute in hierarchy precedence then alphabetical order; configurable timeout (default 5s); fail-open semantics (errors logged, never block); JSON over stdin.

You are a senior Go code reviewer doing an implementation peer review in the AGH greenfield-alpha codebase (agent operating system, AGH Network protocol). READ-ONLY: do not edit any file. Your job is to find defects with exact evidence.

SLICE: internal/network — channel fanout policy activation, mentions, subscriptions/digest/mute delivery, delivery composition diet, digest mode, cost attribution.

Read these files IN FULL (all modified on branch `network-optimization`; also read internal/network/activation.go if it exists — it was added):
- internal/network/router.go
- internal/network/router_test.go
- internal/network/delivery.go
- internal/network/delivery_test.go
- internal/network/envelope.go
- internal/network/manager.go
- internal/network/manager_test.go
- internal/network/validate.go
- internal/network/audit.go
- internal/network/hooks_test.go
- internal/network/transport_test.go
- internal/network/activation.go (new file)

Context — the megaround spec requires:
1. Channel fanout_policy: capability_match (DEFAULT) | coordinator | all_members. For an UNADDRESSED thread message with no recorded participants, evaluate channel policy instead of returning zero deliveries (this REVERSES round 1's zero-delivery default — an intentional hard cut).
2. capability_match: deterministic no-LLM matcher tokenizing SayBody.Intent (fallback Text) against each LocalPeer.CapabilityCatalog ID/Summary. Top-K bounded (default 3). No match → digest fallback to thread/channel members — NEVER silently nothing, NEVER all-members full injection.
3. coordinator: full injection to channel's coordinator_peer_id; missing/unavailable coordinator → digest fallback.
4. Envelope.Mentions []string: KEEP To. Mention-only envelopes STAY on the broadcast subject (subjectForEnvelope must NOT flip to DirectSubject for mention-only). Mentioned peers get full injection + become thread participants. Mentions override policy/mute.
5. Subscriptions: mute|digest|full + keyword filters; most-specific thread row wins over channel row; empty filters = always applicable; mute suppresses only unmentioned/unaddressed.
6. Delivery diet: suppress protocolGuidanceText after first exposure per session via DURABLE ledger (survives reconnect/dropSession); say bodies render as escaped PLAIN TEXT not base64 JSON; structured non-say bodies stay base64 capped by config; digest DeliveryMode coalesces multiple envelopes into one prompt; prompt-cost attribution must be allocated across coalesced envelopes by canonical size (NOT charge each envelope as a full injection).

Hunt for BLOCKERS:
- Concurrency: races on shared maps/state, goroutine leaks, missing context cancellation, lock-ordering hazards. Check any new mutex/map/goroutine in manager.go/router.go/delivery.go.
- Correctness: nil deref on hot path (delivery loop), off-by-one in top-K selection, swallowed errors (`_` discard), subjectForEnvelope incorrectly flipping mention-only to direct subject, mute incorrectly suppressing mentioned/addressed traffic, digest cost attribution charging full injection per envelope.
- Security: raw claim_token crossing transport/log/memory (grep the slice for claim_token), secrets in logs.
- Greenfield violations: dual fields, compat shims, leftover round-1 zero-delivery path not deleted.
- Subject routing: mention-only must NOT become DirectSubject.
- workspace_id: subscription resolution and activation must be workspace-scoped.

For EACH defect:
- SEVERITY: BLOCKER | RISK | NIT
- TITLE
- FILE / LINE
- EVIDENCE: exact code quote (2-8 lines)
- WHY: concrete failure scenario (inputs → wrong output) + rule violated
- FIX

Be concrete and skeptical; do not inflate nits to blockers. Return ALL findings in one structured message. State explicitly if a required behavior (e.g. durable guidance suppression, mention-only broadcast subject, honest digest cost) appears missing or wrong.

149	func (g *GlobalDB) buildNetworkMessageListQuery(
150		ctx context.Context,
151		query store.NetworkMessageQuery,
152	) (string, []any, bool, error) {
153		sqlQuery := `SELECT
154				message_id,
155				session_id,
156				workspace_id,
157				channel,
158			surface,
159			thread_id,
160			direct_id,
161			direction,
162			peer_from,
163			peer_to,
164			kind,
165			work_id,
166			reply_to,
167			trace_id,
168			causation_id,
169			intent,
170			text,
171			preview_text,
172			mentions_json,
173			ext_json,
174			body_json,
175			COALESCE((
176				SELECT MAX(audit.size)
177				FROM network_audit_log AS audit
178				WHERE audit.workspace_id = network_timeline_log.workspace_id
179					AND audit.message_id = network_timeline_log.message_id
180			), 0),
181			timestamp
182		FROM network_timeline_log`
183	
184		where, args := networkMessageFilterClauses(query, true)
185	
186		reverseResults := false
187		switch {
188		case strings.TrimSpace(query.BeforeMessageID) != "":
189			cursor, cursorErr := g.lookupNetworkMessageCursor(ctx, query.BeforeMessageID, query)
190			if cursorErr != nil {
191				return "", nil, false, cursorErr
192			}
193			where = append(where, "(timestamp < ? OR (timestamp = ? AND message_id < ?))")
194			args = append(args, cursor.Timestamp, cursor.Timestamp, cursor.MessageID)
195			reverseResults = true
196		case strings.TrimSpace(query.AfterMessageID) != "":
197			cursor, cursorErr := g.lookupNetworkMessageCursor(ctx, query.AfterMessageID, query)
198			if cursorErr != nil {
199				return "", nil, false, cursorErr
200			}
201			where = append(where, "(timestamp > ? OR (timestamp = ? AND message_id > ?))")
202			args = append(args, cursor.Timestamp, cursor.Timestamp, cursor.MessageID)
203		}
204	
205		sqlQuery = store.AppendWhere(sqlQuery, where)
206		if reverseResults {
207			sqlQuery += " ORDER BY timestamp DESC, message_id DESC"
208		} else {
209			sqlQuery += " ORDER BY timestamp ASC, message_id ASC"
210		}
211		sqlQuery, args = store.AppendLimit(sqlQuery, args, query.Limit)
212		return sqlQuery, args, reverseResults, nil
213	}

215	func networkMessageFilterClauses(query store.NetworkMessageQuery, includeMessageID bool) ([]string, []any) {
216		messageID := ""
217		if includeMessageID {
218			messageID = query.MessageID
219		}
220		where, args := store.BuildClauses(
221			store.StringClause("workspace_id", query.WorkspaceID),
222			store.StringClause("session_id", query.SessionID),
223			store.StringClause("channel", query.Channel),
224			store.StringClause("peer_from", query.PeerFrom),
225			store.StringClause("peer_to", query.PeerTo),
226			store.StringClause("kind", query.Kind),
227			store.StringClause("direction", query.Direction),
228			store.StringClause("message_id", messageID),
229			store.TimeClause("timestamp", ">=", query.Since),
230		)
231		if peerID := strings.TrimSpace(query.PeerID); peerID != "" {
232			where = append(where, "(peer_from = ? OR peer_to = ?)")
233			args = append(args, peerID, peerID)
234		}
235		if query.DirectedOnly {
236			where = append(where, "peer_to IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(peer_to) <> ''")
237		}
238		return where, args
239	}

242		entries := make([]store.NetworkMessageEntry, 0)
243		for rows.Next() {
244			entry, err := scanNetworkMessage(rows)
245			if err != nil {
246				return nil, err
247			}

249		}

252		}

256	func reverseNetworkMessages(entries []store.NetworkMessageEntry) {
257		for left, right := 0, len(entries)-1; left < right; left, right = left+1, right-1 {
258			entries[left], entries[right] = entries[right], entries[left]
259		}
260	}

263		ctx context.Context,
264		messageID string,
265		query store.NetworkMessageQuery,

285			}
286			return networkMessageCursor{}, fmt.Errorf("store: lookup network message cursor: %w", err)
287		}

33			ctx,
34			`SELECT workspace_id, channel, thread_id, peer_id, first_message_id, first_seen_at, last_seen_at
35			FROM network_thread_participants
36			WHERE workspace_id = ? AND channel = ? AND thread_id = ?
37			ORDER BY last_seen_at DESC, peer_id ASC`,

407	func (g *GlobalDB) UpdateTaskRun(ctx context.Context, run taskpkg.Run) error {
408		if err := g.checkReady(ctx, "update task run"); err != nil {
409			return err
410		}

413		if err != nil {

415		}

417		return g.withTaskImmediateTransaction(ctx, "update task run", func(exec taskSQLExecutor) error {
418			current, err := g.getTaskRunWithExecutor(ctx, exec, normalized.ID)
419			if err != nil {
420				return err
421			}
422			currentSessionID := strings.TrimSpace(current.SessionID)
423			nextSessionID := strings.TrimSpace(normalized.SessionID)
424			if currentSessionID != "" &&
425				nextSessionID != currentSessionID &&
426				(nextSessionID != "" || normalized.Status.Normalize() != taskpkg.TaskRunStatusQueued) &&
427				!allowsManagedTaskRunStartSessionTransfer(current, normalized) {
428				return taskpkg.ErrSessionAlreadyBound

430			if normalized.QueuedAt.IsZero() {
431				normalized.QueuedAt = current.QueuedAt
432			}
433			if err := g.ensureTaskExistsWithExecutor(ctx, exec, normalized.TaskID); err != nil {
434				return err
435			}
436			if err := updateTaskRunRecordWithExecutor(ctx, exec, normalized); err != nil {
437				return err
438			}
439			if err := updateTaskCurrentRunProjectionForRunUpdate(ctx, exec, current, normalized); err != nil {
440				return err
441			}
442			return replaceTaskRunCapabilitiesWithExecutor(ctx, exec, normalized)
443		})
444	}

505	func allowsManagedTaskRunStartSessionTransfer(current taskpkg.Run, next taskpkg.Run) bool {
506		currentStatus := current.Status.Normalize()
507		nextStatus := next.Status.Normalize()
508		currentSessionID := strings.TrimSpace(current.SessionID)
509		if strings.TrimSpace(next.SessionID) == "" {
510			return false
511		}
512		if current.ClaimedBy == nil ||
513			current.ClaimedBy.Kind.Normalize() != taskpkg.ActorKindAgentSession ||
514			strings.TrimSpace(current.ClaimedBy.Ref) != currentSessionID {
515			return false
516		}
517		if currentStatus == taskpkg.TaskRunStatusClaimed && nextStatus == taskpkg.TaskRunStatusStarting {
518			return true
519		}
520		return currentStatus == taskpkg.TaskRunStatusStarting &&
521			nextStatus == taskpkg.TaskRunStatusStarting &&
522			current.StartedAt.IsZero() &&
523			next.StartedAt.IsZero()
524	}

957			ctx,
958			`SELECT run_id, capability_id FROM `+table+`
959			 WHERE run_id IN (`+strings.Join(placeholders, ", ")+`)
960			 ORDER BY run_id ASC, capability_id ASC`,

962		)
963		if err != nil {

966		defer func() {

968		}()
969	
970		result := make(map[string][]string, len(runIDs))
971		for rows.Next() {

974			if err := rows.Scan(&runID, &capabilityID); err != nil {
975				return nil, fmt.Errorf("store: scan %s capability row: %w", table, err)
976			}
977			result[runID] = append(result[runID], capabilityID)

No swallowed errors, no `ORDER BY 0`. My review is complete. Let me compile my findings.

## Peer Review Findings — Persistence Layer (migrations v43–v47 + store methods)

I read all 15 target files in full, plus the migration runner (`schema.go`), the SQLite open path (`sqlite.go`), the tx helpers, and the downstream callers of every new store method. Overall the slice is high quality: migrations are correctly append-only, all new tables/columns use numbered migrations (no `EnsureSchema`-for-columns), workspace scoping is consistent across the new network tables, and the state-mutating multi-statement paths use `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`.

Below are the findings, most-severe first. None are BLOCKERs.

---

### 1. RISK — `network_subscribe`/`network_mute` can hit an unguarded FK constraint failure
- FILE: `internal/daemon/native_tools.go`
- LINE: 1776 (write); FK defined in `internal/store/globaldb/global_db.go:174`
- EVIDENCE (`global_db.go` `networkSubscriptionsTableStatement`):
  ```
  FOREIGN KEY (workspace_id, channel)
      REFERENCES network_channels(workspace_id, channel)
      ON DELETE CASCADE
  ```
  `networkSetSubscription` builds the entry and calls `PutNetworkSubscription` directly with no prior `network_channels` existence check. FKs are enforced (`internal/store/sqlite.go:123` `foreign_keys(ON)`).
- WHY: If an agent calls `network_subscribe`/`network_mute`/`network_digest_mode` for a channel string that has no persisted `network_channels` row (a channel only ever seen as ephemeral message traffic, a typo, or a not-yet-created channel), the `INSERT INTO network_subscriptions` fails with `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`, surfaced to the agent as a generic `nativeNetworkInputError` with an opaque SQLite message. The FK correctly prevents orphan subscriptions (no data leak), but the agent-facing failure mode is unclear and there is no test covering the "subscribe before channel exists" path. This is a robustness/agent-manageability gap, not a data-integrity defect.
- FIX: Either (a) upsert a `network_channels` row (or verify existence and return a clear domain error like "channel not found; create it first") before `PutNetworkSubscription`, or (b) map the FK error to a typed `ErrNetworkChannelNotFound` in the store method so the transport returns a deterministic 404/validation error. Add a canonical test in the subscriptions suite for the missing-channel case.

---

### 2. NIT — Pre-existing workspace-agnostic channel lookup now carries the new columns (out-of-slice, low risk)
- FILE: `internal/store/globaldb/global_db_task_claim.go`
- LINE: 935 (`networkChannelEntry`)
- EVIDENCE:
  ```
  `SELECT channel, workspace_id, purpose, fanout_policy, coordinator_peer_id, created_by, created_at, updated_at
   FROM network_channels
   WHERE channel = ?`,
  ```
- WHY: This lookup filters by `channel` only, not `(workspace_id, channel)`, so a same-named channel in another workspace could match. This slice only extended the SELECT with `fanout_policy`/`coordinator_peer_id`; the workspace-agnostic predicate is pre-existing (introduced in PR #75). Practical risk is negligible because `coordination_channel_id` values are run-derived/unique, and `ensureQueuedRunCoordinationChannel` (`global_db_task_aux.go:885`) explicitly re-checks `entry.WorkspaceID == trimmedWorkspaceID` after the lookup. Flagging only so the workspace-scoping debt is recorded; not introduced by this megaround.
- FIX: When touched next, add `AND workspace_id = ?` to `networkChannelEntry` and thread the run's workspace_id through `coordinationChannelMetadata`.

---

### 3. NIT — `task_designation_rollups` is currently a write-only table (no production reader)
- FILE: `internal/store/globaldb/global_db_network_preferences.go`

## Peer Review: `internal/network` — Channel Fanout Policy Activation, Mentions, Subscriptions/Digest/Mute, Delivery Diet

**Scope note:** `internal/network/activation.go` does not exist on branch `network-optimization` — the activation logic lives inline in `router.go` (`selectActivatedThreadPeers`, `rankActivationCandidates`, `activationScore`, `activationTerms`). The megaround changes are split across a "savepoint" commit plus a large body of **uncommitted** working-tree edits.

Verdict: **REWORK.** Several load-bearing megaround requirements are either missing or contradict the spec, and the entire subscription/digest/activation surface ships with zero test coverage.

---

### BLOCKER 1 — Channel `fanout_policy` (capability_match | coordinator | all_members) is entirely unimplemented
- **FILE:** `internal/network/router.go:1208-1272` (and absent across `internal/config`, `internal/store`)
- **EVIDENCE:** `grep` for `fanout_policy|FanoutPolicy|coordinator_peer_id|capability_match|all_members` returns **nothing** in `internal/network`, `internal/config`, `internal/store`. `deliveriesFromLocalPeers` unconditionally calls `selectActivatedThreadPeers(...)` for every unaddressed empty/unresolved thread:
```go
if len(participants) == 0 {
    return deliveriesFromLocalPeers(r.selectActivatedThreadPeers(peers, envelope, nil, mentioned), envelope), nil
}
```
- **WHY:** Spec requires a per-channel `fanout_policy` with three modes, defaulting to `capability_match`, plus a `coordinator` mode routing to `coordinator_peer_id`. None of that exists. There is no policy field, no coordinator routing, no per-channel selection. An unaddressed empty-thread message always runs the same keyword top-K matcher regardless of any policy. The `coordinator` fanout mode and its digest fallback are completely absent.
- **FIX:** Introduce the channel `fanout_policy` config/store field and `coordinator_peer_id`; branch delivery selection on the resolved policy; implement `coordinator` full-injection + digest fallback.

### BLOCKER 2 — capability_match "no match → digest fallback" is instead full injection (spec says NEVER all-members full injection)
- **FILE:** `internal/network/router.go:1234-1272`, delivered as `Delivery{...}` with empty `Mode` → forced to `full` in `manager.go:1155`
- **EVIDENCE:** `activationScore` returns `0` for all peers when there is no term overlap (or an undecodable body → `activationTerms` returns `nil`). `selectActivatedThreadPeers` still fills up to `activationTopK` peers by PeerID order and returns them as normal deliveries. `applyDeliverySubscriptions` then sets `next.Mode = store.NetworkSubscriptionModeFull`. Router test `router_test.go:436-499` asserts a **full delivery** to the sole channel peer for an empty thread with no capability match.
- **WHY:** Spec: "No match → digest fallback to thread/channel members — NEVER silently nothing, NEVER all-members full injection." Current behavior injects the *full* message to the top-K (all, when peers ≤ K) channel members with score 0. That is exactly the "all-members full injection" the spec forbids, and it is never downgraded to digest.
- **FIX:** When the matcher yields no positive-score peers, emit deliveries with `Mode = digest` to the fallback member set rather than full injection.

### BLOCKER 3 — Digest DeliveryMode does not coalesce; cost is charged as a full injection per envelope
- **FILE:** `internal/network/delivery.go:595-651` (`runWorker`/`processQueuedItem`), `delivery.go:653-666` (`deliveredPromptCostForMessage`), `manager.go:1885-1923` (`recordThreadPeerPromptCost`)
- **EVIDENCE:** `runWorker` dequeues one `queuedEnvelope` at a time and `processQueuedItem` renders + prompts each individually; `cost := deliveredPromptCostForMessage(message)` sets `PromptSizeBytes = int64(len(message))` for that single rendered prompt, and `recordThreadPeerPromptCost` writes `DeliveredCount: 1, PromptSizeBytes: cost.PromptSizeBytes` per envelope. Config keys `DigestFlushInterval` / `DigestMaxEnvelopes` (`config.go:468-469`, defaults 250ms/10, validated at `config.go:1745-1749`) are **never read** anywhere in `internal/network`.
- **WHY:** Spec: "digest DeliveryMode coalesces multiple envelopes into one prompt; prompt-cost attribution must be allocated across coalesced envelopes by canonical size (NOT charge each envelope as a full injection)." There is no coalescing loop and no flush timer; each digest envelope becomes its own prompt and is billed the full rendered size. `manager_test.go:505-532` confirms a single delivery is charged its entire `PromptSizeBytes=512`.
- **FIX:** Implement digest batching driven by `DigestFlushInterval`/`DigestMaxEnvelopes`, render one coalesced prompt, and split the prompt cost across member envelopes by canonical body size.

### BLOCKER 4 — `mute` incorrectly suppresses *addressed* (directed) traffic
- **FILE:** `internal/network/manager.go:1179-1239` (`deliverySubscriptionMode`), applied to all deliveries in `applyDeliverySubscriptions` (`manager.go:1147-1169`)
- **EVIDENCE:** The only exemption before consulting subscriptions is *mention*:
```go
if deliveryMentionsPeer(delivery.Envelope, delivery.PeerID) {
    return store.NetworkSubscriptionModeFull, nil
}
```
There is no `delivery.Envelope.IsDirected()` / `To == peer` exemption. A directed say (`To = reviewer.sess-b`) reaches `applyDeliverySubscriptions`, and if that peer has a channel/thread `mute` row, `deliverySubscriptionMode` returns `mute` and the delivery is dropped (`continue` at `manager.go:1161-1162`).
- **WHY:** Spec: "mute suppresses only unmentioned/**unaddressed**." A muted peer who is directly addressed will silently never receive the message — a correctness/lost-message defect.
- **FIX:** Add an addressed exemption (`if delivery.Envelope.IsDirected() && *To == delivery.PeerID { return Full }`) alongside the mention exemption.

### RISK 5 — Blocking SQLite read held under the delivery mutex
- **FILE:** `internal/network/delivery.go:514-526` (`guidanceModeForDelivery`)
- **EVIDENCE:** `c.mu.Lock()` is held while calling `c.guidanceStore.GetNetworkDeliveryGuidanceState(c.lifecycleCtx, target)`, which is a synchronous `QueryRowContext` (`internal/store/globaldb/global_db_network_preferences.go:154`). The same `c.mu` guards `acceptOne`→`notifyWaiters`, `queueForSession`, `markInFlight`, `dropSession`, `stats`, and `queueDepthMetrics`.
- **WHY:** On the first delivery per session (both guidance flags false) a contended/slow global-DB read blocks *all* inbound accept/enqueue and stats across every session on the daemon. Bounded (once per session) but a real lock-during-IO hazard under load or DB contention.
- **FIX:** Read the durable guidance state outside the lock, then re-acquire `c.mu` only to memoize.

### RISK 6 — Entire subscription/digest/activation surface has zero test coverage
- **FILE:** `internal/network/*_test.go`
- **EVIDENCE:** `grep` across all network test files for `deliverySubscriptionMode|firstApplicableSubscription|subscriptionKeywordFiltersMatch|ListNetworkSubscriptions|NetworkSubscriptionModeMute|NetworkSubscriptionModeDigest|applyDeliverySubscriptions|formatNetworkDigestMessage|selectActivatedThreadPeers|rankActivationCandidates|activationScore` returns **no matches**. `manager_test.go` has no `Test…Subscription/Mute/Digest/Keyword` functions.
- **WHY:** Most-specific-thread-row-wins, empty-filters-always-apply, keyword filtering, mute/digest resolution, digest rendering, and capability scoring are all shipped unverified. Given the correctness defects above, this is not incidental — the invariants are unowned.
- **FIX:** Add canonical suite(s) covering subscription mode precedence (thread > channel), keyword-filter match/miss, mute-suppresses-only-unmentioned/unaddressed, digest rendering, and activation top-K ordering/fallback-to-digest.

### RISK 7 — `DeliveryStructuredBodyMaxBytes` cap is unenforced
- **FILE:** `internal/network/delivery.go:1122-1168` (`formatNetworkMessageWithDeliveryMode`)
- **EVIDENCE:** `grep DeliveryStructuredBodyMaxBytes` in non-test network code: none. The renderer base64-encodes the full canonical body (`encodedBody = base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(deliveryBody.canonicalBody)`) with no size cap. The config key is defined/validated (`config.go:469,1748`) and surfaced through settings only (`api/core/conversions.go:2327`).
- **WHY:** Spec: "structured non-say bodies stay base64 capped by config." The cap is a dead config knob; oversized structured bodies inject uncapped.
- **FIX:** Truncate/cap the base64-encoded structured body at `DeliveryStructuredBodyMaxBytes` (with a truncation marker), or delete the config key if the cap is not intended.

- **Mention-only stays on broadcast subject.** `subjectForEnvelope` (`router.go:1166-1171`) branches only on `IsDirected()` (`To != nil`); `Mentions` never flips to `DirectSubject`. Mentioned peers get full injection and are added to the delivery set (`router.go:1227`, `1250`), and mention exempts mute (`manager.go:1187`). Correct.
- **`To` kept, `Mentions []string` added.** No dual fields / compat shims; round-1 `return nil, nil` zero-delivery path is deleted (confirmed via committed vs. working-tree diff). Clean hard cut.
- **Raw `claim_token` / secret defense intact.** `validateEnvelopeContainsNoRawSecrets` (`validate.go:623-730`) scans body/proof/ext; `mentions` is a `[]string` of peer IDs normalized via `NormalizeNetworkPeerIDs`. No raw-token leak path introduced.
- **workspace-scoping.** Thread participant resolution (`router.go:1369-1388`) and subscription queries (`manager.go:1202-1231`) both carry `WorkspaceID`. Correct.
- **Durable guidance suppression works** (modulo RISK 5): reads durable store on cold cache, persists on delivery, survives `dropSession` (in-memory entry deleted, DB row retained). Note: the terse `protocolGuidanceText` lines (incl. the direct-room line) are intentionally *retained* in compact mode — only the verbose bash examples are suppressed (`delivery.go:1294-1300`, asserted by `delivery_test.go:442-471`). func activationScore(peer LocalPeer, terms []string) int {
	if len(terms) == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	var builder strings.Builder
	builder.WriteString(strings.Join(peer.PeerCard.Capabilities, " "))
	for _, capability := range peer.CapabilityCatalog {
		builder.WriteByte(' ')
		builder.WriteString(capability.ID)
		builder.WriteByte(' ')
		builder.WriteString(capability.Summary)
		builder.WriteByte(' ')
		builder.WriteString(capability.Outcome)
	}
	haystack := strings.ToLower(builder.String())
	score := 0
	for _, term := range terms {
		if strings.Contains(haystack, term) {
			score++
		}
	}
	return score
}

func mentionedPeerSet(envelope Envelope) map[string]bool {
	mentions := normalizeEnvelopeMentions(envelope.Mentions)
	if len(mentions) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	set := make(map[string]bool, len(mentions))
	for _, peerID := range mentions {
		set[strings.TrimSpace(peerID)] = true
	}
	return set
}

772	// UnmarshalJSON rejects legacy public network send fields during request decoding.
773	func (r *NetworkSendRequest) UnmarshalJSON(data []byte) error {
774		type networkSendRequestAlias NetworkSendRequest
775		var raw map[string]json.RawMessage
776		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &raw); err != nil {
777			return err
778		}
779		if _, ok := raw["interaction_id"]; ok {
780			return errors.New("network send request rejects interaction_id; use work_id")
781		}
782	
783		var decoded networkSendRequestAlias
784		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &decoded); err != nil {
785			return err
786		}
787		if strings.TrimSpace(decoded.Kind) == contractDirectKey {
788			return errors.New("network send request rejects kind direct; use surface direct with kind say")
789		}
790		*r = NetworkSendRequest(decoded)
791		return nil
792	}

109	func (h *BaseHandlers) taskActorContextForWorkspace(
110		c *gin.Context,
111		action string,
112		expectedWorkspaceID string,
113	) (taskpkg.ActorContext, error) {
114		if h.TaskActorContextResolver != nil {
115			return h.TaskActorContextResolver(c, action)
116		}
117		credentials := agentCallerCredentialsFromRequest(c)
118		if hasAgentCallerIdentityCredentials(credentials) {
119			caller, err := h.resolveAgentCallerForWorkspace(
120				c.Request.Context(),
121				credentials,
122				"tasks."+strings.TrimSpace(action),
123				expectedWorkspaceID,
124			)
125			if err != nil {
126				return taskpkg.ActorContext{}, err
127			}
128			return caller.Actor, nil
129		}
130		return taskpkg.DeriveHumanActorContext(
131			defaultTaskActorRef,
132			taskOriginKindForTransport(h.transportName()),
133			"tasks."+strings.TrimSpace(action),
134		)
135	}
136	
137	func taskOriginKindForTransport(name string) taskpkg.OriginKind {
138		normalized := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(name))
139		switch {
140		case strings.Contains(normalized, "uds"):
141			return taskpkg.OriginKindUDS
142		case strings.Contains(normalized, "web"):
143			return taskpkg.OriginKindWeb
144		case strings.Contains(normalized, "cli"):
145			return taskpkg.OriginKindCLI
146		default:
147			return taskpkg.OriginKindHTTP
148		}
149	}

875		transportQuery, err := ParseTaskStreamQuery(c)
876		if err != nil {

880		query, err := h.taskStreamDomainQuery(c, transportQuery)

1141	func (h *BaseHandlers) FanOutTaskRuns(c *gin.Context) {
1142		manager, ok := h.requireTaskManager(c)
1143		if !ok {

1145		}
1146		networkStore, err := h.networkStoreRequired()
1147		if err != nil {

1149			return
1150		}
1151		taskID, err := requiredPathID(c.Param("id"), "task id")
1152		if err != nil {
1153			h.respondError(c, StatusForTaskError(err), err)
1154			return
1155		}
1156		var req contract.FanOutTaskRunsRequest
1157		if err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&req); err != nil {
1158			h.respondError(
1159				c,
1160				http.StatusBadRequest,
1161				NewTaskValidationError(fmt.Errorf("%s: decode fan-out task runs request: %w", h.transportName(), err)),
1162			)
1163			return
1164		}
1165		maxDesignations := h.Config.Task.Orchestration.DesignatedRunMax
1166		if maxDesignations <= 0 {
1167			maxDesignations = 5
1168		}
1169		if err := validateFanOutTaskRunsRequest(req, maxDesignations); err != nil {
1170			h.respondError(c, StatusForTaskError(err), err)
1171			return
1172		}
1173		actor, err := h.taskActorContext(c, taskActionFanOutRuns)
1174		if err != nil {

1176			return
1177		}
1178		groupID := store.NewID("tdg")
1179		runs, err := enqueueFanOutTaskRuns(c.Request.Context(), manager, actor, taskID, groupID, req)
1180		if err != nil {
1181			h.respondError(c, StatusForTaskError(err), err)
1182			return
1183		}
1184		now := h.nowUTC()
1185		if err := networkStore.PutTaskDesignationRollup(

1187			store.TaskDesignationRollup{
1188				DesignationGroupID: groupID,
1189				TaskID:             taskID,
1190				SummaryJSON:        fanOutDesignationRollupJSON(runs, now),
1191				CreatedAt:          now,
1192			},
1193		); err != nil {

1195			return
1196		}

1199			Runs:               TaskRunPayloadsFromRuns(runs),

1203	func validateFanOutTaskRunsRequest(req contract.FanOutTaskRunsRequest, maxDesignations int) error {
1204		if len(req.Designations) == 0 {
1205			return NewTaskValidationError(errors.New("designations are required"))
1206		}
1207		if len(req.Designations) > maxDesignations {
1208			return NewTaskValidationError(fmt.Errorf("designations cannot exceed %d", maxDesignations))
1209		}
1210		return validateTaskChannel("fan_out_runs.network_channel", req.NetworkChannel)
1211	}

1213	func enqueueFanOutTaskRuns(
1214		ctx context.Context,
1215		manager TaskService,
1216		actor taskpkg.ActorContext,
1217		taskID string,
1218		groupID string,
1219		req contract.FanOutTaskRunsRequest,
1220	) ([]taskpkg.Run, error) {
1221		runs := make([]taskpkg.Run, 0, len(req.Designations))
1222		for index, designation := range req.Designations {
1223			metadata, err := fanOutDesignationMetadata(index, designation)
1224			if err != nil {
1225				return nil, err
1226			}
1227			run, err := manager.EnqueueRun(ctx, taskpkg.EnqueueRun{
1228				TaskID:             taskID,
1229				IdempotencyKey:     fanOutDesignationIdempotencyKey(req.IdempotencyKey, designation, index),
1230				NetworkChannel:     strings.TrimSpace(req.NetworkChannel),
1231				DesignationGroupID: groupID,
1232				Metadata:           metadata,
1233			}, actor)
1234			if err != nil {
1235				return nil, err
1236			}
1237			runs = append(runs, *run)
1238		}
1239		return runs, nil
1240	}

372			return UpdateNetworkChannelRequest{}, errors.New(
373				"cli: at least one of --purpose, --fanout-policy, or --coordinator-peer-id is required",

375		}
376		return request, nil

379	func resolveNetworkCreateChannelName(args []string, channelFlag string) (string, error) {
380		fromArg := ""
381		if len(args) == 1 {
382			fromArg = strings.TrimSpace(args[0])
383		}
384		fromFlag := strings.TrimSpace(channelFlag)
385		switch {
386		case fromArg == "" && fromFlag == "":
387			return "", errors.New("cli: channel is required")
388		case fromArg != "" && fromFlag != "" && fromArg != fromFlag:
389			return "", errors.New("cli: channel argument and --channel must match")
390		case fromArg != "":
391			return fromArg, nil
392		default:
393			return fromFlag, nil
394		}
395	}

607	func (o *Observer) taskHealthFromSnapshot(
608		ctx context.Context,
609		snapshot taskSnapshot,
610		summary Summary,
611		metrics TaskMetrics,
612	) (TaskHealth, error) {
613		stuckRuns := findStuckRuns(snapshot.runs, o.now(), o.taskHealthConfig)
614		sortStuckRuns(stuckRuns)
615		activeOrphans, err := o.countActiveOrphanRuns(ctx, snapshot.runs)
616		if err != nil {
617			return TaskHealth{}, err
618		}
619	
620		queueDepthTotal := 0
621		var oldestQueuedAt time.Time
622		var oldestQueuedAge int64
623		for _, item := range summary.QueueDepth {
624			queueDepthTotal += item.Count
625			if item.OldestQueuedAt.IsZero() {
626				continue
627			}
628			if oldestQueuedAt.IsZero() || item.OldestQueuedAt.Before(oldestQueuedAt) {
629				oldestQueuedAt = item.OldestQueuedAt
630				oldestQueuedAge = item.OldestQueueAgeMilli
631			}
632		}
633	
634		status := taskHealthStatusOK
635		if len(stuckRuns) > 0 || activeOrphans > 0 {
636			status = taskHealthStatusWarn
637		}
638	
639		return TaskHealth{
640			Status:                     status,
641			QueueDepthTotal:            queueDepthTotal,
642			OldestQueuedAt:             oldestQueuedAt,
643			OldestQueueAgeMilli:        oldestQueuedAge,
644			QueueDepth:                 summary.QueueDepth,
645			StuckRuns:                  stuckRuns,
646			ActiveOrphanRuns:           activeOrphans,
647			TaskTotals:                 summary.TaskTotals,
648			RunTotals:                  summary.RunTotals,
649			OwnerTotals:                summary.OwnerTotals,
650			ForcedStopsSinceStart:      metrics.TaskForcedStopsTotal,
651			DuplicateIngressSinceStart: metrics.DuplicateIngressTotal,
652			ChannelMismatchSinceStart:  metrics.ChannelMismatchTotal,
653			RecoverySinceStart:         metrics.RecoveryTotals,
654		}, nil
655	}

783	func taskDashboardStatusBreakdownFromTotals(totals TaskDashboardTotals) []TaskDashboardStatusBreakdown {
784		type statusCount struct {
785			status taskpkg.Status
786			count  int
787		}
788	
789		rows := []statusCount{
790			{status: taskpkg.TaskStatusCompleted, count: totals.CompletedTasks},
791			{status: taskpkg.TaskStatusPending, count: totals.PendingTasks},
792			{status: taskpkg.TaskStatusInProgress, count: totals.InProgressTasks},
793			{status: taskpkg.TaskStatusReady, count: totals.ReadyTasks},
794			{status: taskpkg.TaskStatusBlocked, count: totals.BlockedTasks},
795			{status: taskpkg.TaskStatusFailed, count: totals.FailedTasks},
796			{status: taskpkg.TaskStatusCanceled, count: totals.CanceledTasks},
797			{status: taskpkg.TaskStatusDraft, count: totals.DraftTasks},
798		}
799	
800		breakdown := make([]TaskDashboardStatusBreakdown, 0, len(rows))
801		for _, row := range rows {
802			if row.count <= 0 || totals.TasksTotal <= 0 {
803				continue
804			}
805			breakdown = append(breakdown, TaskDashboardStatusBreakdown{
806				Status:       row.status,
807				Count:        row.count,
808				SharePercent: int(math.Round(float64(row.count) * 100 / float64(totals.TasksTotal))),
809			})
810		}
811		return breakdown
812	}

814	func taskDashboardQueueFromRows(
815		rows []TaskQueueDepth,
816		cfg taskDashboardConfig,
817		now func() time.Time,
818	) TaskDashboardQueue {
819		queue := TaskDashboardQueue{
820			Depth: rows,
821		}
822		threshold := max(cfg.backlogWarnAfter, 0)
823		queue.BacklogThresholdMilli = threshold.Milliseconds()
824	
825		for _, item := range rows {
826			queue.Total += item.Count
827			if item.OldestQueuedAt.IsZero() {
828				continue
829			}
830			if queue.OldestQueuedAt.IsZero() || item.OldestQueuedAt.Before(queue.OldestQueuedAt) {
831				queue.OldestQueuedAt = item.OldestQueuedAt
832				queue.OldestQueueAgeMilli = item.OldestQueueAgeMilli
833			}
834		}
835	
836		if queue.Total > 0 && threshold > 0 && time.Duration(queue.OldestQueueAgeMilli)*time.Millisecond >= threshold {
837			queue.BacklogWarning = true
838			queue.BacklogStatus = taskHealthStatusWarn
839		} else {
840			queue.BacklogStatus = taskHealthStatusOK
841		}
842		if now != nil && !queue.OldestQueuedAt.IsZero() {
843			queue.OldestQueueAgeMilli = safeSince(now(), queue.OldestQueuedAt).Milliseconds()
844			if queue.Total > 0 && threshold > 0 && time.Duration(queue.OldestQueueAgeMilli)*time.Millisecond >= threshold {
845				queue.BacklogWarning = true
846				queue.BacklogStatus = taskHealthStatusWarn
847			}
848		}
849	
850		return queue
851	}

926	func taskInboxFromSnapshot(
927		snapshot taskSnapshot,
928		triageStates []taskpkg.TriageState,
929		query TaskInboxQuery,
930		actor taskpkg.ActorIdentity,
931	) TaskInboxView {
932		triageByTaskID := taskInboxTriageByTaskID(triageStates)
933		runsByTaskID := taskRunsByTaskID(snapshot.runs)
934		eventsByTaskID := taskEventsByTaskID(snapshot.events)
935		lanes := taskInboxLanes(query.Lane.Normalize())
936		itemsByLane := make(map[TaskInboxLane][]TaskInboxItem, len(lanes))
937		countsByLane := make(map[TaskInboxLane]int, len(lanes))
938		unreadByLane := make(map[TaskInboxLane]int, len(lanes))
939	
940		view := TaskInboxView{}
941		selectedLane := query.Lane.Normalize()
942		for _, summary := range snapshot.tasks {
943			taskID := strings.TrimSpace(summary.ID)
944			if taskID == "" {
945				continue
946			}
947	
948			taskRuns := runsByTaskID[taskID]
949			taskEvents := eventsByTaskID[taskID]
950			latestActivityAt := taskInboxLatestActivityAt(summary, taskRuns, taskEvents)
951			triage, hasTriage := triageByTaskID[taskID]
952			effectiveTriage := taskInboxEffectiveTriage(taskID, actor, latestActivityAt, triage, hasTriage)
953			if taskInboxSuppressedByDismissal(effectiveTriage) {
954				continue
955			}
956	
957			latestRun := latestTaskInboxRun(taskRuns)
958			lane, include := taskInboxLaneForTask(summary, latestRun, taskRuns, effectiveTriage, actor)
959			if !include {
960				continue
961			}
962			if selectedLane != "" && lane != selectedLane {
963				continue
964			}
965	
966			item := TaskInboxItem{
967				Task:             taskInboxReference(summary),
968				Lane:             lane,
969				ApprovalPolicy:   summary.ApprovalPolicy,
970				ApprovalState:    summary.ApprovalState,
971				BlockingReason:   taskInboxBlockingReason(summary, latestRun),
972				LatestActivityAt: latestActivityAt,
973				Run:              taskInboxRunSummary(latestRun, summary.MaxAttempts),
974				Triage:           effectiveTriage,
975			}
976			if query.Unread && !taskInboxItemUnread(item) {
977				continue
978			}
979	
980			countsByLane[lane]++
981			if taskInboxItemUnread(item) {
982				unreadByLane[lane]++
983				view.UnreadTotal++
984			}
985			if lane == TaskInboxLaneArchived {
986				view.ArchivedTotal++
987			}
988			view.Total++
989			itemsByLane[lane] = append(itemsByLane[lane], item)
990		}
991	
992		view.Groups = taskInboxGroups(lanes, itemsByLane, countsByLane, unreadByLane, query.Limit)
993		return view
994	}

133		seen := make(map[HarnessAugmenter]struct{}, len(descriptors))
134		for _, descriptor := range descriptors {

136			if name == "" {

138			}

141			}
142			if descriptor.Augmenter == nil {

144			}

146			normalized = append(normalized, promptInputAugmenterDescriptor{
147				Name:           name,

149				Budget:         max(descriptor.Budget, 0),
150				BudgetBehavior: normalizePromptInputAugmenterBudgetBehavior(descriptor.BudgetBehavior),
151				Critical:       descriptor.Critical,
152				Augmenter:      descriptor.Augmenter,
153			})

157		slices.SortStableFunc(normalized, func(left, right promptInputAugmenterDescriptor) int {
158			if left.Order != right.Order {
159				return left.Order - right.Order
160			}
161			return strings.Compare(string(left.Name), string(right.Name))

455		total := 0
456		for _, descriptor := range descriptors {

459			}
460			total += descriptor.Budget

465	func applyPromptInputAugmenterBudget(
466		current string,
467		next string,
468		limited bool,
469		remainingBudget int,
470		behavior promptInputAugmenterBudgetBehavior,
471	) (string, int) {
472		if !limited {
473			return next, promptInputContributionRunes(current, next)
474		}
475		if remainingBudget <= 0 {
476			return current, 0
477		}
478	
479		before, after, wrapped := splitPromptInputAugmentation(current, next)
480		if wrapped {
481			contribution := utf8.RuneCountInString(before) + utf8.RuneCountInString(after)
482			if contribution <= remainingBudget {
483				return next, contribution
484			}
485			if normalizePromptInputAugmenterBudgetBehavior(behavior) == promptInputAugmenterBudgetBehaviorOmit {
486				return current, 0
487			}
488	
489			beforeBudget := min(utf8.RuneCountInString(before), remainingBudget)
490			trimmedBefore := trimStringToRunes(before, beforeBudget)
491			trimmedAfter := trimStringToRunes(after, remainingBudget-beforeBudget)
492			return strings.TrimSpace(trimmedBefore + current + trimmedAfter), remainingBudget
493		}
494	
495		contribution := promptInputContributionRunes(current, next)
496		if contribution <= remainingBudget {
497			return next, contribution
498		}
499		if normalizePromptInputAugmenterBudgetBehavior(behavior) == promptInputAugmenterBudgetBehaviorOmit {
500			return current, 0
501		}
502		return current, 0
503	}
504	
505	func splitPromptInputAugmentation(current string, next string) (string, string, bool) {
506		if current == "" {
507			return "", "", false
508		}
509	
510		before, after, ok := strings.Cut(next, current)
511		if !ok {
512			return "", "", false
513		}
514		return before, after, true
515	}
516	
517	func promptInputContributionRunes(current string, next string) int {
518		before, after, wrapped := splitPromptInputAugmentation(current, next)
519		if wrapped {
520			return utf8.RuneCountInString(before) + utf8.RuneCountInString(after)
521		}
522		return max(utf8.RuneCountInString(next)-utf8.RuneCountInString(current), 0)
523	}

238	func bundledReferencesPromptSectionProvider(name string, referencePaths ...string) session.PromptProvider {
239		return promptSectionProviderFunc(func(context.Context, *workspacepkg.ResolvedWorkspace) (string, error) {
240			contents := make([]string, 0, len(referencePaths))
241			for _, referencePath := range referencePaths {
242				content, err := skillbundled.LoadResource(strings.TrimSpace(name), strings.TrimSpace(referencePath))
243				if err != nil {
244					return "", fmt.Errorf(
245						"daemon: load bundled startup section %q file %q: %w",
246						name,
247						referencePath,
248						err,
249					)
250				}
251				contents = append(contents, strings.TrimSpace(content))
252			}
253			return strings.Join(contents, "\n\n"), nil
254		})

259	// Resolve derives one authoritative harness context from explicit inputs.
260	func (r *HarnessContextResolver) Resolve(input HarnessResolutionInput) (ResolvedHarnessContext, error) {
261		if r == nil {
262			return ResolvedHarnessContext{}, errors.New("daemon: harness context resolver is required")
263		}
264	
265		surface := normalizeResolutionSurface(input.Surface)
266		if surface == "" {
267			return ResolvedHarnessContext{}, fmt.Errorf("daemon: invalid harness resolution surface %q", input.Surface)
268		}
269	
270		sessionCtx, err := normalizeHarnessSessionContext(input.Session)
271		if err != nil {
272			return ResolvedHarnessContext{}, err
273		}
274	
275		turnCtx, err := r.normalizeHarnessTurnContext(sessionCtx, input.Turn)
276		if err != nil {
277			return ResolvedHarnessContext{}, err
278		}
279	
280		policy := ResolvedHarnessPolicy{
281			SessionClass:     sessionCtx.SessionClass,
282			TurnOrigin:       turnCtx.Origin,
283			IncludeSections:  r.resolveSections(sessionCtx),
284			EnableAugmenters: r.resolveAugmenters(surface, turnCtx),
285			ReentryMode:      r.resolveReentry(turnCtx),
286			DetachedRunMode:  r.resolveDetachedRunMode(sessionCtx, turnCtx),
287		}
288		policy.DiagnosticLabel = buildHarnessDiagnosticLabel(sessionCtx, policy)
289		policy.ObservabilityTags = buildHarnessObservabilityTags(surface, sessionCtx, turnCtx, policy)
290	
291		return ResolvedHarnessContext{
292			Surface: surface,
293			Session: sessionCtx,
294			Turn:    turnCtx,
295			Policy:  policy,
296		}, nil
297	}

494	func (d *Daemon) bootLockAndSocket(
495		ctx context.Context,
496		state *bootState,
497		cleanup *bootCleanup,
498	) error {
499		pid := d.pid()
500		lock, err := d.acquireLock(d.homePaths.DaemonLock, pid)
501		if err != nil {
502			return err
503		}
504		cleanup.add(func(context.Context) error {
505			return lock.Release()
506		})
507		state.lock = lock
508	
509		if stalePID := d.resolveStaleDaemonPID(lock, pid, state.logger); stalePID > 0 {
510			if cleanupErr := d.cleanupOrphans(ctx, stalePID); cleanupErr != nil {
511				state.logger.Warn(
512					"daemon: cleanup orphan processes failed",
513					"stale_pid",
514					stalePID,
515					"error",
516					cleanupErr,
517				)
518			}
519		}
520	
521		if err := removeStaleSocket(state.cfg.Daemon.Socket); err != nil {
522			return err
523		}
524		return nil
525	}

527	func (d *Daemon) resolveStaleDaemonPID(lock *Lock, pid int, logger *slog.Logger) int {
528		if lock == nil {
529			return 0
530		}
531		if stalePID := lock.StalePID(); stalePID > 0 {
532			return stalePID
533		}
534	
535		existingInfo, err := ReadInfo(d.homePaths.DaemonInfo)
536		switch {
537		case err == nil && existingInfo.PID > 0 && existingInfo.PID != pid && !d.processAlive(existingInfo.PID):
538			return existingInfo.PID
539		case err != nil && !errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) && logger != nil:
540			logger.Warn(
541				"daemon: read stale daemon info failed",
542				"path",
543				d.homePaths.DaemonInfo,
544				"error",
545				err,
546			)
547		}
548		return 0
549	}
